title: Sheinbaum Confirms Resumption of Mexican Cattle Exports to the US
author: Alonso Urrutia and Alma Muñoz
content:
_This article by Alonso Urrutia and Alma Muñoz originally appeared in the[July
24, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/07/24/economia/sheinbaum-
confirma-reanudacion-de-las-exportaciones-de-ganado-mexicano-a-eu), Mexico’s
premier left wing daily newspaper._

President Claudia Sheinbaum reported that, through a letter from the United
States Secretary of Agriculture, Brooke Rollins, the reopening of the border
to Mexican cattle was formalized, so that starting in August the export of
Mexican production will resume.

Through her social media, Sheinbaum Pardo detailed that, following the
official U.S. notification, she instructed the Secretary of Agriculture and
Rural Development to accelerate “even further the work and collaboration with
the United States to have everything ready as quickly as possible to restart
the movement of cattle.**Exports will resume starting in the last weeks of the
month of August through Agua Prieta, Sonora, followed shortly after by two
additional points in the state of Chihuahua.”**

> Me da mucho gusto informar al pueblo de México y especialmente a las y los
> ganaderos de nuestro país, que hoy recibí una carta de la secretaria de
> Agricultura de Estados Unidos, Brooke Rollins, en la que me informa la
> decisión de su gobierno de reanudar la exportación de ganado…
>
> -- Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo (@Claudiashein) [July 25,
> 2026](https://x.com/Claudiashein/status/2080814274587300084?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

The resurgence of the screwworm plague in Mexico and its growth prompted the
United States to cancel the importation of Mexican cattle on May 11, 2025,
affecting mainly ranchers in the north of the country.

The president considered that Rollins’s letter represents great news for
Mexican ranchers.****

> “I recognize the effort they have made over many months to contain the
> screwworm plague, collaborating with the Secretariat of Agriculture and
> Rural Development and the National Service of Agri-Food Health, Safety, and
> Quality (Senasica).”

She gave particular recognition to the former head of Sader, Julio Berdegué,
and to Columba López, the current head of the agency, for their great effort
to achieve the reopening of the border.
